findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this bucket (including the uploaded vendor roster) have no enforced SSE-KMS/AES256 default.
No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is attached, so the bucket lacks any explicit guardrail against public ACLs or policy grants.
No logging block is configured, so access to the vendor/report data is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic reconstruction of unauthorized access.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced default encryption.
No logging block is defined for this ledger data bucket, leaving no S3 access trail of object reads or modifications.
Protection relies solely on the private ACL; no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block prevents a later ACL or policy change from exposing ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket configures versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so public ACLs or bucket policies could still be applied to it.
No default server-side encryption is configured for the runbooks bucket, which typically holds sensitive operational procedures, endpoints, and infrastructure detail.
No logging block is configured, so reads of runbook content are not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket from accidental public ACL or policy exposure.
The centralized audit/log-delivery bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so highly sensitive access logs are not explicitly shielded from any public ACL or policy grant.

The bucket holding audit logs for other buckets sets force_destroy = true and has no object lock or MFA delete, so log evidence can be deleted by anyone with write or Terraform access, undermining audit trail integrity.

The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so potentially sensitive third-party data lands in S3 unencrypted; the file is also carried in the repository.
